name: Smallest number that is the sum of 3 cubes of primes in exactly n different ways.
comment: In the SageMath code, B > 326, is sufficient to conclude the correctness of the 5th term (a(5) < P[327]^3) and B > 168 to confirm the first 4 values.
For the 6th term, one needs B > 1001 implying a(6) > 499243435237.
example: a(1) = 24, since 24 = 2^3 + 2^3 + 2^3 (unique way) is the smallest sum of prime cubes.

a(5) = 10588881419, since it is the smallest number which is sum of 3 primecubes in 5 ways, it can be obtained with the following triples: {59, 1669, 1811}, {83, 1567, 1889}, {139, 1427, 1973}, {349, 1091, 2099} and {479, 929, 2131}.
program: M=[i for i in d.keys() if d[i]==5]
author: _Stijn Cambie_, Sep 20 2025
